title: Platform access token: JWT header and claims an IAM member issues
description: Issuer side of the access token, iam/1.0 (TOKENS.md). Stricter than what a verifier requires (be-protocol P5, schemas/access-token.schema.json there): a verifier accepts aud as a string or an array and ignores unknown claims; an IAM member emits exactly this. Cross-field rules JSON Schema cannot state are in TOKENS.md: exp - iat <= 3600 (default 600), nbf == iat, aud[0] == TENANT_ID, iss == IAM_ISSUER, ceil and dg present together and only with act.

aud.description: An array whose first element is TENANT_ID. Further audiences are reserved (a future external API audience); none is emitted in iam/1.0.

roles.description: Role codes from the authorization provider's ResolveClaims at login and refresh (contract-infra-authz). Omitted when the user has no role; never permission keys (decision 0203).

dept_path.description: The user's department path from ResolveClaims, /<id>/<id>/.../. Omitted when the user has no department; never the empty string and never "/" (be-protocol P6.4).

ceil.description: Ceiling profile codes of an act_as delegation (contract-infra-authz profiles). Only with act and dg.

dg.description: The delegation grant id from the authorization provider's CreateDelegation. Only with act and ceil.

azp.description: The platform client the token was issued to (pc, mobile, ...), mapped by the member from the IdP client id; for a service account, svc.

locale.description: BCP 47. Omitted when the user has none; the component then uses the deployment default.

subject.description: A platform user id (UUIDv7), or svc:<id> for a service account (reserved).

actor.description: The acting party (RFC 8693 section 4.1), nestable: act.act is the party that acted before. kind agent is reserved (A4): no member issues it in iam/1.0.
